subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop propagating broad host workspace overrides such as `path-to-regexp` into third-party managed npm plugin roots, or should it keep the current override propagation and only detect/report Express 4 conflicts?
rationale: Both paths affect the plugin dependency ownership contract and security override policy: preserving plugin dependency graphs may reduce central security pin reach, while keeping propagation can break third-party plugins at runtime.

options.title: Scope managed-root overrides
options.body: Adjust managed npm roots so plugin-owned dependency ranges are not overridden by unrelated host pins such as `path-to-regexp`, while preserving explicit security pins that are safe for plugin graphs.

options.title: Add detection only
options.body: Keep host override propagation but detect Express 4 plus incompatible `path-to-regexp` resolution during install/update and fail with an actionable error.

options.title: Document plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Declare that third-party Express 4 plugins must ship their own override or migrate to Express 5, and update docs without changing core install behavior.

recommendation.title: Scope managed-root overrides
recommendation.body: Adjust managed npm roots so plugin-owned dependency ranges are not overridden by unrelated host pins such as `path-to-regexp`, while preserving explicit security pins that are safe for plugin graphs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current managed npm override code and related lockfile/workspace override lines are in this person's recent authored history.
